callers.note: census only; the enclosing function's role is not pinned
census only; post-call code checks the return value and the out slice's first byte

detail_builder.role: builds the 'prefix: detail' string into a heap buffer stored at the out struct +0x08; the window frees that buffer unread

decision_byte.source: the callee stores its rsi argument (2) there; the window parses only when the byte is 0
decision_byte.consequence: on the detail path the parse branch is unreachable in node #94; the arm always reports 'could not decode SetCompressionType record' and loops

compression_arm.note: the arm clears the accumulator and stores the loop-head snapshot to reader +0x58 before the length/tag checks, but does NOT reset the in-fragment flag; a later last fragment therefore finalizes with only the post-compression fragments, and the success offset is the compression arm's snapshot

parser.input: body struct whose first byte is the tag
parser.tag_reading: 0 and 7 are the accepted tags in this binary; the names behind them are not pinned from the bytes

success_paths.effect: parser runs, arm loops with first-snapshot updated to this arm's snapshot

arguments.rcx: transform out-pointer, passed through from this window's 5th argument

codes.0..9: record type byte (0 zero, 1 full, 2 first, 3 middle, 4 last, 5..8 recyclable, 9 set-compression)
codes.11: trailer (zero type, zero length) or stream failure
codes.12: leftover too short for a header after the final block; leftover size written to the remaining out-pointer
codes.14: header plus payload past remaining buffer; remaining size written to the out-pointer
codes.15: CRC mismatch; remaining size written to the out-pointer
codes.above_15: treated by this window as an unknown record type

10.not_in_fragment: return False, no report, no clear
10.in_fragment_strict_modes_1_2: report 'error reading trailing data' with accumulator length, clear, return False

other_loop.11: report 'error in middle of record' with accumulator length and clear when in-fragment, then reset and loop

12.strict_modes_1_2: report 'truncated header' with remaining size, then when in-fragment report 'error reading trailing data' with accumulator length and clear; return False
12.other_modes: clear when in-fragment, return False, no report

13.in_fragment_strict_modes_1_2: report 'error reading trailing data' with accumulator length, clear, return False

short_final_set.strict_modes_1_2: report 'truncated record body' with remaining size, return False, accumulator NOT cleared

short_final_clear.mode_nonzero: report 'bad record length' with remaining size, then error-in-middle continuation, then loop
short_final_clear.mode_zero_sticky_clear: report 'bad record length' with remaining size, then error-in-middle continuation, then loop

15.sticky_clear: report 'checksum mismatch' with remaining size, then error-in-middle continuation, then loop
15.sticky_set_mode_nonzero: report 'checksum mismatch' with remaining size, then error-in-middle continuation, then loop

other_loop.error_in_middle_continuation: when in-fragment, report 'error in middle of record' with accumulator length and clear; then reset and loop
other_loop.unknown: format 'unknown record type %u' into a 40-byte stack buffer, report it with fragment length plus accumulator length when in-fragment, clear, reset, loop

skip_loop_mode_3.10_12: clear when in-fragment, return False, no report
skip_loop_mode_3.11_13: report 'error in middle of record' with accumulator length and clear when in-fragment, then reset and loop

14.short_final_set: return False, no report, no clear
14.short_final_clear: report 'bad record length' with remaining size, then error-in-middle continuation, then loop

skip_loop_mode_3.15: report 'checksum mismatch' with remaining size, then error-in-middle continuation, then loop
skip_loop_mode_3.unknown: same as the other loop's unknown arm, looping to the skip-loop head

first.in_fragment_nonempty: report 'partial record without end(2)' with accumulator length, then stream reset (called even with a null stream object; the callee guards null)
first.stream_mode: append fragment to the +0xa8 stream object when transform out-pointer is non-null
first.effect: accumulator replaced by the fragment, in-fragment set, first-snapshot stored, loop

full.in_fragment_nonempty: report 'partial record without end(1)' with accumulator length
full.transform: when transform out-pointer is non-null and reader +0x78 is null, one-shot transform of the fragment, result stored to the out-pointer; suppressed when +0x78 is non-null
full.effect: accumulator cleared, out slice = fragment slice, success offset = current loop-head snapshot, seen flag set, return True

last.not_in_fragment: report 'missing start of fragmented record(2)' with fragment length, reset, loop
last.stream_mode: append fragment to the +0xa8 stream object, then finish it, result stored to the transform out-pointer
last.effect: fragment appended to accumulator with the 0x3fffffffffffffff cap check, out slice = accumulator contents, success offset = first-snapshot, seen flag set, return True

middle.not_in_fragment: report 'missing start of fragmented record(1)' with fragment length, reset, loop
middle.stream_mode: append fragment to the +0xa8 stream object when transform out-pointer is non-null
middle.effect: fragment appended to accumulator with the 0x3fffffffffffffff cap check, loop (first-snapshot untouched)

mode_byte.argument: low byte of the 4th argument, saved to stack rsp+0x2f

branches.3: skip loop entered at function entry
branches.1_2: strict reporting arms in the other loop ((mode - 1) <= 1 unsigned)
branches.0: tolerate arms in the other loop

mode_byte.inferred_reading: the branch pattern matches the WAL recovery-mode pattern (0 tolerate, 1/2 strict, 3 skip-and-continue); the enum names are an inference from the behavior, not bytes in the packet, and every condition above is pinned without them

callers_observed.0x50ca36d: a byte from the caller's struct at +0x4a2

prologue.accumulator_string: the 3rd argument string is cleared (length 0, first byte 0)
prologue.attached_hook: when reader +0x78 is non-null, its vtable +0x18 slot is called with the object in rdi; the window does not set rsi/rdx before the call, so the callee's arity is not pinned
prologue.out_slice: the 2nd argument slice is reset to (ptr 0x1e629b, len 0)
prologue.stream_object: when the transform out-pointer is non-null, the +0xa8 object is created via 0x543bde0 when null, then reset via 0x543be50

reader_fields.+0x40: bytes remaining in the decode buffer
reader_fields.+0x48: short-final-block flag, set by the refill helper
reader_fields.+0x58: success offset snapshot, written on success (current snapshot for full records, first-snapshot for fragmented records, compression-arm snapshot on compression records)
reader_fields.+0x60: cumulative bytes supplied by the refill helper
reader_fields.+0x70: sticky flag, set by decode when a recyclable header is seen while cumulative equals remaining
reader_fields.+0x71: seen flag, set to 1 on every successful return
reader_fields.+0x72: compression type byte, written by the body parser
reader_fields.+0x73: compression-seen flag, written by the body parser
reader_fields.+0x78: attached object, created by the body parser; presence suppresses the full-record one-shot transform
reader_fields.+0x80: 0x8000-byte buffer, allocated by the body parser
reader_fields.+0xa8: stream object for the transform path, created lazily in the prologue

reporter.note: the reporter itself builds a Corruption status (code 2) from the message via 0x542f040 and forwards it through 0x5160f40; the status construction inside the compression arm is a separate call to the same builder

return_values.0: end of data or an error return (see the error arms)
return_values.1: a logical record was assembled; the out slice holds it
